front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text:
This Surah is named Al-Fatihah because of its subject-matter. Fatihah is opening, whether it be a subject or a book or any other thing else. In other words, Al-Fatihah is a preface or introduction.
Other names of this Surah include but are not limited to: Al-Hamd (The Praise), As-Salah (The Prayer), Umm al-Kitab (Mother of the Book), Umm al-Quran (Mother of the Quran), Sab'a min al-Mathani (Seven Repeated Ones, from Quran 15:87), and Ash-Shifa' (The Cure).

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: This is a Makki Surah and the first complete Surah that was revealed to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). Before this, only a few Ayat’s were revealed which form parts of `Alaq, Muzzammil, Muddaththir, etc.

front_matter.label: Subject and Topics
front_matter.text:
This Surah is in fact a prayer/dua which Allah SWT has taught all those who want to learn/read His book. Surah Al-Fatihah is a prayer/dua for guidance.
Thus, the real relation between Al-Fatihah and the Quran is not that of an introduction to a book rather a prayer and its answer. Al-Fatihah is the prayer from the servant and the Quran is the answer from the Master. The servant makes dua to Allah SWT to show him guidance and the Master places the whole of the Quran before him in answer to his prayer, as if to say, "This is the Guidance you begged from Me."

sections.title: GROUP 1: OPENING: THE REQUEST FOR GUIDANCE

translation.text: In the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate

commentary.text: Before beginning anything, one should adopt the principle of reciting the Basmalah or بِسۡمِ اللهِ الرَّحۡمٰنِ الرَّحِيۡمِ

One of the most important benefits is that when one begins something by reciting Allah SWT’s name, he/she will enjoy Allah SWT’s support and aid; Allah SWT will bless his/her efforts and protect him/her from the conspiracies and temptation of satan. For whenever man turns to Allah SWT, Allah SWT turns to him/her as well.

translation.text: Praise be to Allah, the Lord of the entire universe.

commentary.text: The nature of this surah is that of a dua/prayer -- a dua/prayer that begins with the praise of the One to whom our dua is being addressed to. This principle indicates that whenever one prays one ought to pray in a dignified manner and not blurt out his/her petition.  Thus, the etiquette of dua is mentioned here.

اَلۡحَمۡدُ لِلّٰهِ means -- ALL praise + ALL thanks belong to Allah SWT exclusively. The entire universe, the angels are all praising Allah SWT – all the time. Allah SWT does not need our worthless praise rather it is only to our benefit/advantage that we recognize who our Creator is and just as importantly thank Him for each and every one of our blessings including the breath we just took.

translation.text: The Merciful, the Compassionate

commentary.text: Whenever we are impressed by something we express our feelings via superlatives and often we tend to re-emphasize our awe by adding an additional superlative. This would seem to explain the use of the word Ar-Rahman followed by Ar-Rahim.

The root word for Ar-Rahman and Ar-Rahim are  ra-ha-meem, which literally means the ‘womb’ of a mother. Allah SWT is more Rahman/Rahim than 70 mothers. Allah SWT mercy and compassion towards his creators is so expansive and infinite in its nature that it has no bounds. Having said, our minds are not capable of turly understanding the magnitude of Allah SWT mercy and compassion and only Allah SWT is fully aware of the true meanings.

translation.text: The Master of the Day of Judgement

commentary.text: The description of Allah SWT as the Master of the Day of Judgement following the mention of His kindness and compassion indicates that we must remember another aspect of Allah SWT as well that on the Day of Judgement no one will have the power either to resist the enforcement of punishments that He decrees or to prevent anyone from receiving the rewards that He decides to confer.

Hence, we ought not only to love Him for nourishing and sustaining us and for His compassion and mercy towards us, but should also hold Him in reverence because of His justice, and should not forget that our ultimate happiness or misery rests completely with Him.
Allah is Al-Malik (King or Owner)
Yawm Ad-Din is the Day of Recompense for the creatures, meaning the Day of Judgment.
Thus far the above Ayat’s are an introduction to Allah SWT’s attributes and Majesty. Now in the next Ayat’s we are talking directly to Allah SWT (Allah SWT is always listening).

translation.text: You alone do we worship, and You alone do we turn for help

commentary.text: This is our declaration to Allah SWT to worship Him alone and turn to help to Him alone. The first part is a declaration of innocence from Shirk (polytheism), while the second negates having any power or strength, displaying the recognition that all affairs are controlled by Allah alone.

The term ibadah/worship denotes: (i) worship and respect; (ii) obedience and submission; and (iii) service and subjection. In this particular context the term carries all three meanings simultaneously. In other words, man's worship and total devotion, man's unreserved obedience, and man's absolute subjection and servitude are exclusively for his Raab and Creator.

Not only do we worship Allah SWT, but our relationship with Him is such that we turn to Him alone for help. That is, we do not turn to any others whether it is people, money, status, power, etc., in seeking the fulfillment of our needs. We know that He is the Lord of the whole universe and that He alone is the Master of all blessings and benefactions. It is in Him that we place our trust and Him alone that we address our request for true guidance.

translation.text: Direct/guide us on to the Straight Way

commentary.text: Now that we have arrived at the point where we recognize our Raab along with the certainty of a Hereafter, and we have declared an oath to worship only Allah SWT and seek help only from Allah SWT. -- then we ask Allah SWT to lead/direct us to the correct way of life – a way that will yield for us true and eternal salvation and happiness.

This is man’s prayer/dua to Allah SWT as he begins the study of the Quran. To illuminate the truth and enlighten him as to which of the myriad ways and by-ways is the clear, straight, open road of sound belief and right behavior.
Each and every issue or matter that man will face on earth is dealt with in the Quran -- for our guidance.
A believer asks for guidance every hour of every day so as to help him remain firm/steady on the straight path and so that Allah SWT may increase our understanding/knowledge.

arabic_lines: صِرَاطَ الَّذِيۡنَ اَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ۙ‏ غَيۡرِ الۡمَغۡضُوۡبِ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا الضَّآلِّيۡنَ

translation.text: The path of those You have blessed, those who incur no anger and who have not gone astray.

commentary.text: صِرَاطَ الَّذِيۡنَ اَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ refers to the ‘straight path ‘of those upon whom You have granted Your grace (show us the way of such people). The way which has always been followed by those who have enjoyed God's favors and blessings.  Those upon whom Allah has bestowed His grace' include: (i) the Prophets (ii) those devoted to truthfulness (iii) the martyrs (iv) and the righteous.
SURAH AN-NISA AYAT 69 AND 70
(4:69) And guided them to a straight path.

(4:70) And he who obeys Allah and the Messenger -they shall be with those whom Allah has favoured -the Prophets, those steadfast in truthfulness, the martyrs, and the righteous." How excellent will they be for companions!

He who enjoys, in this world, the company of the kind of people mentioned in the Ayat above, and whom God judges worthy of the same company in the Hereafter is fortunate. Good/pious people have always longed for the company of like people, both in this world and the Next. The companionship of corrupt and sinful people is a painful punishment even in this transient world, let alone their perpetual companionship in the Hereafter.

This also makes it clear that the recipients of God's favour are not the Pharaohs, and Korahs (Qaruns) of the past or present who appear, briefly, to enjoy worldly prosperity and success; rather it is Iman, and righteous conduct through which one gains Allah SWT’s approval and pleasure leading to the ultimate success.
People of guidance, sincerity and obedience to Allah and His Messengers are the people who adhere to Allah's commandments and refrain from committing what He has prohibited.

غَيۡرِ الۡمَغۡضُوۡبِ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا الضَّآلِّيۡنَ. And help us avoid the path of those (i) who know the truth, yet deviate from it. Also, help us avoid the path of those (ii) who lost the true knowledge and, as a result, are wandering in misguidance, unable to find the correct path.

These are people who received anger – Allah SWT is angry with them, the angels are angry with them, the believers are angry with them, their future generations are angry with them. 
Thus, anger is hurled at them from all directions.
Saying Ameen: It is recommended to say Ameen after finishing the recitation of Al-Fatihah. Ameen means,
"O Allah! Accept our invocation."

Lesson: Understand the majesty of our Raab, seek guidance/help from Allah SWT alone, implement His guidance with sincerity and obedience via actions. Look for role models in the past and be aware of your company today.

THE SIGNIFICANCE AND STATUS OF SURAH AL- FATIHAH

A basic philosophy of Islam is that we are all born upon the fitra, that is, we all have instinctual or potential guidance within us as to what is right and what is wrong. All scriptures, including the Quran, help activate/awaken this dormant consciousness.
Human nature is such that even without revelations or Prophets we can come to some basic assumptions:
(Pls refer to Surah Luqman)

There is a Creator – That this entire universe and its contents did not just come into existence by accident rather there is a Maker/Creator who is ensuring the existence along with the exact balance for everything.
This world is but transitory. The real and final destination is the Hereafter where each will be fully compensated for their deeds and misdeeds.

Upon arriving at these two conclusions man then seeks guidance as to the straight path because as humans, we can assume a thing bad that is good and vice vera -- leading to disaster consequences. (Important to note that it is not for man to dictate or decide right from wrong or vice versa).

AH now that we are of those who have understood the majesty of our Raab and that very soon we will have to face our Raab therefore Surah Al- Fatihah is the dua for guidance so that we may gain success (Paradise).

Note: In addition to our higher nature or fitra in Islam we also have an animalistic/lower nature with cardinal desires. These instincts and desires are blind as they want nothing but immediate gratification making no difference where it is halal or haram -- we need to control these blind instincts and subjugate them to Allah SWT’s will and laws.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text:
Why the name Al-Baqara?
Al-Baqara (the Cow) is from the story of the Cow (Ayat 67-73), it is not, however, a title to indicate the subject of the Surah.

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text:
Though a Madani Surah, it follows naturally a Makki Surah Al- Fatihah, which ended with the prayer: "Show us the straight way." It begins with the answer to that prayer, "This is the Book (that)...is guidance..."
Revealed over two years in Madinah after the migration of the Prophet (PBUH) in 622.  By now two-thirds of the Quran had been revealed in Mecca.

front_matter.label: Subject and Topics
front_matter.text: This Surah is an invitation to Divine Guidance and all the stories, incidents etc., revolve round this central theme. This Surah has been mainly addressed to the Jews; therefore, many historical events have been cited from their own traditions to admonish and advise them that their own good rests in accepting the Guidance revealed to the Holy Prophet. They should, therefore, be the first to accept it because it was basically the same that was revealed to Prophet Musa (PBUH).

front_matter.label: Historical Background:
front_matter.text:
In order to understand the meaning of this Surah, we need to understand that historical background/context:
JEWS
In Makkah the Quran generally addressed the mushrik Quraish who were ignorant of Islam, but in Madinah it also addressed the Jews who were acquainted with the creed of Tawhid, Prophethood, Revelation, the Hereafter and Angels. Although the Jews believed in the law which was revealed by Allah SWT to their Prophet Musa (PBUH) and in principle, their way was the same (Islam) that was being taught by Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). But they had strayed and adopted many un-Islamic creeds, rites and customs of which there was no mention nor sanction in the Torah.
In addition; they had tampered with the Torah by inserting their own explanations and interpretations into its text. They had distorted the real spirit of true religion and were now clinging to a lifeless frame of rituals.
Consequently, their beliefs, their morals and their conduct had gone to the lowest depths of degeneration but they had no intention or inclination to accept any kind of reform. So, they became bitter enemies of those who came to teach them the Right Way.
This was their religious condition when the Holy Prophet (PBUH) went to Madinah and invited the Jews to the true religion. That is why more than one third of this Surah has been addressed to the Children of Israel with a critical review of their history, their moral degeneration and their religious perversions.
HYPOCRITES
During this period, a new type of "Muslim," munafiqin (hypocrites), had begun to appear.
There were some who had entered the Islamic fold merely to harm it from within. There were others who were surrounded by Muslims and, therefore, had become "Muslims" to safeguard their worldly interests. They, therefore, continued to have relations with the enemies so that if the latter became successful, their interests should remain secure. There were still others who had no strong conviction of the truth of Islam but had embraced it along with their clan. Lastly, there were those who were intellectually convinced of the truth of Islam but did not have enough moral courage to give up their former traditions, superstitions and personal ambitions and live up to the Islamic moral standards and make sacrifice in its way.
At the time of the revelation of Al-Baqarah, all sorts of hypocrites had begun to appear. Allah SWT has, therefore, briefly pointed out their characteristics here.
MADANI SURAH THEME OF LAWS AND SOCIAL REFORM
In Makkah Islam was mainly concerned with the propagation of its fundamental principles and the moral training of its followers. But after the migration of the Holy Prophet to Madinah, where Muslims had come to settle from all over Arabia and a tiny Islamic State had been set up with the help of the Ansar (local supporters), naturally the Quran had to turn its attention to the social, cultural, economic, political and legal problems as well. This accounts for the difference between the themes of the Surahs revealed at Makkah and those in Madinah. Accordingly, about half of this Surah deals with those principles and regulations which are essential for the integration and solidarity of a community and for the solution of its problems.
JIHAD
After the migration to Madina, Muslims from all parts of Arabia came and settled as one community, and established an independent city state which all of non- Muslim Arabia was united upon crushing totally. Hence for its very survival, the following instructions were revealed in this Surah:
The Community should work with the utmost zeal. Infuse courage and fortitude in its adherents (the majority of whom were homeless and indigent and surrounded on all sides by enemies) needed for the eradication of evil ways and for the establishment of the Islamic Way instead.
Prepare them to meet and oppose any armed menace, without heeding to the overwhelming numerical strength and the material resources of its enemies.

translation.text: Alif, Lam, Mim.

commentary.text: The names of letters of the Arabic alphabet that occur at the beginning of several surahs of the Quran are called ‘Huruf Muqatta’t’ or ‘Disjointed letters.’

translation.text: This is the Book of Allah, there is no doubt in it; it is a guidance for the pious,

commentary.text: One obvious meaning of this Ayat is that the Quran, is undoubtedly from God. Another possible meaning is that nothing contained in it can be subject to doubt.
Surah Al- Fatihah, ended with the prayer: "Show us the straight way."

Now begins the answer to that prayer, "This is the Book (that)...is guidance..." A guidance for the pious or ‘Al Mutaqeen’ or those who have taqwa. Taqwa, means Allah consciousness with both fear + love of our Lord. Linguistically the word ‘taqwa,’ means a ‘shield or protective barrier’, as taqwa is derived from the word ‘waqa’ which means to protect, safeguard or shield.
Example that demonstrates or defines the meaning of ‘Taqwa’
When Umar Ibn Al-Khattab هasked Ubay Ibn Ka’ab about Taqwa.
Ubay said, “Have you ever taken a thorny path?”
Umar replied, “Yes I have.”
Ubay then asked, “So how did you travel along this thorny path?”
Umar replied, “I rolled up my garment and was cautious as to where I would tread to avoid being pricked by the thorns.”
So Ubay responded and said, “This is Taqwa.”
Lesson: A Momin navigates/ treads through this world with caution and is fully cognizant of Allah SWT’s likes and dislikes.
Whereas the Quran is potentially for all, yet only those who possess certain qualities can benefit from it.

The first quality is virtue, goodness, piety, thus, those who want to benefit should be disposed to distinguish between good and evil. Conversely, those who never consider whether their actions are either good or bad and are helplessly tossed about by animalistic desires are infact incapable of deriving any benefit from the guidance embodied in the Quran.

translation.text: who believe in the unseen, establish prayer, and donate from what We have provided for them,

commentary.text: The second quality is belief in the unseen, i.e. Allah SWT, the Angels or Jinns, Heaven/Hell etc. It is imperative to have a strong belief in these or else our entire world view or behavior will change.
The third quality is to establish regular and proper prayer as the Prophet (PBUH) has taught us.
The fourth quality is to spend on others in Allah SWT’s way in good causes.

translation.text: and who believe in what has been revealed to you ˹O Prophet˺ and what was revealed before you, and have sure faith in the Hereafter.

commentary.text: The fifth quality is those who believe in ALL the divine scriptures.
The sixth quality is those who have a strong, sure and firm conviction that indeed there will be a time where we will be held accountable for our actions and then rewarded or not for them.

translation.text: As for those who persist in disbelief, it is the same whether you warn them or not—they will never believe.

arabic_lines: خَتَمَ اللّٰهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوۡبِهِمۡ وَعَلٰى سَمۡعِهِمۡ​ؕ وَعَلٰىٓ اَبۡصَارِهِمۡ غِشَاوَةٌ وَّلَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ عَظِيۡمٌ

translation.text: God has sealed their hearts and their ears, and their eyes are covered. They will have great torment.

commentary.text: The (i) first group of people mentioned above (Ayat 2,3,4 and 5) are the Believers.
Now the (ii) second group is being mentioned: The Non-Believers.

This is a difficult Ayat to understand, that is, if you warn them or do not warn them these people will not believe. This clearly does not refer to every non-believer as then there would be no point of giving dawah, however, this refers to a very particular group; those who even after you warn them, they still don’t believe, in fact, they become more adamant, arrogant and stubborn in their kufur/disbelief.  It is only then that Allah SWT puts a seal on their heart – as a punishment.

The sad effects of sin: The first time is hardest as we are born on fitra but then it becomes much easier to sin and one sin leads to another. Eventually we stop feeling bad as repeated sins desensitize us – this is the sealing of our hearts.
Lesson: Iman/faith is a gift therefore do not take it lightly and ask Allah SWT to keep you firm on Islam.
Learn this dua for steadfastness in religion:
يَا مُقَلِّبَ الْقُلُوبِ ثَبِّتْ قَلْبِي عَلَى دِينِكَ
“Oh turner of the hearts (Allah, the Most High), keep our hearts firm on your religion.“

sections.title: 8-16 HYPOCRITES AND THE CONSEQUENCES OF HYPOCRISY

translation.text: There are some who say: “We believe in Allah and in the Last Day,” while in fact they do not believe.
When they meet the believers, they say: “We believe,” but when they meet their evil companions (in privacy), they say: “Surely we are with you; we were merely jesting.”

commentary.text: Now the (iii) third group of people are being mentioned: The Hypocrites.

They say they believe; however, they are deceiving everyone including themselves. There is a fundamental weakness in their character as they sway between belief and disbelief, thus wanting both this life and the Hereafter. They adopt Iman but readily revert to disbelief if they feel their worldly interests are being compromised.

Lesson: There is no compulsion in religion otherwise the concept of this world as a place of test/trials cannot be applied. Allah SWT makes our intentions and desire easy for us, i.e. If we lean towards sin then sin becomes less daunting and if we want lean towards piety or taqwa then, in sha Allah, opportunities in this regard will open up. Remember to never compromise on faith for the temporary benefits of this world. The real life is the life of the Hereafter.

arabic_lines: يٰۤاَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اعۡبُدُوۡا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِىۡ خَلَقَكُمۡ وَالَّذِيۡنَ مِنۡ قَبۡلِكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُوۡنَ ۙ

translation.text: O humanity! Worship your Lord, Who created you and those before you, so that you may become mindful ˹of Him˺.

commentary.text: All mankind is being addressed here in the Quran. The command is to enslave yourself to your Raab by recognizing your Raab and then submitting to Him by worshiping and obeying Him alone. This Ayat encapsulates the core philosophy of the Quran and the basic preaching of each Prophet and Messenger of Allah SWT i.e. the concept of Tauhid.

Lesson: A universal call urging us to reflect upon our Creator and the divine favors bestowed on us and respond by worship and mindfulness. This call speaks to the innermost need of our soul so that we can attain spiritual fulfillment and attain a connection with the divine. Mankind has been created to worship Allah SWT -- this is our purpose in life. It is important to note that the term worship is not exclusive to simply the rituals of salah, roza, Haj etc., -- as we do not perform these rituals 24/7.

The worship of Allah SWT implies a constant (24/7) subservience, and enslavement to our Raab.  Thus, eating, sleeping, playing, working, all should be performed with the full acknowledgment, understanding and appreciation for our Creator.

arabic_lines: وَبَشِّرِ الَّذِيۡنَ اٰمَنُوۡا وَ عَمِلُوا الصّٰلِحٰتِ

translation.text: And give good news (O Muhammad), to those who believe in this Book and do good deeds (in accordance with its teachings). For them there will be gardens underneath which canals flow. sections.title: 27 THE MEANING OF LOSS – AS DEFINED BY ALLAH SWT

translation.text: those who violate Allah’s covenant after it has been affirmed, break whatever ˹ties˺ Allah has ordered to be maintained, and spread corruption in the land. It is they who are the ˹true˺ losers.

commentary.text: DEFINITION OF LOSS ( الۡخٰسِرُوۡن)
Here the term ‘الۡخٰسِرُوۡنَ losers’ refers to whoever decreases his/her own share of Allah's mercy by disobeying Him.
Below are the qualities الۡخٰسِرُوۡنَ losers as defined by Allah SWT in this Ayat.
Those who break the sacred covenant or ‘Ehd e Alsat’ (see background note below) and declared themselves or others as masters.
They cut the ties of kinship or blood relations.
Those who spread unrest and division in this world.
There is a one relationship between God and man and then another between man and man.
The right of God is that we acknowledge Him as our ultimate and exclusive Master.
The right of man is that we treat each other well and not cut the ties of kinship i.e. siblings, parents, aunts, uncles, cousins etc.
Thus, those who do not give (i) God His due (ii) or mankind but especially close blood relations their due are those who cause vice and harm in this world.

Silat ur Rahim means: being generous, kind and maintaining ties with blood relations esp. those who have severed the bond of kinship. FYI – Rahim relations are those of the womb meaning blood relations.

Background note: We all took our first Ehd or Covenant with Allah SWT, called ‘Ehd e Alsat’, before we were ever sent to earth (although no one remembers this). In ‘Alam e Arwa’ all humanity was gathered together before Allah SWT where we acknowledged Allah SWT as our Raab, our Master, our Creator. After taking this Covenant we were put to sleep (our first death). Then we are born and our second and final death is of the human kind.
FYI – At around 120 days of conception an Angel comes and blows life into the womb/fetus.

translation.text: He is the One Who created everything in the earth for you. Then He turned towards the heaven, forming it into seven heavens. And He has ˹perfect˺ knowledge of all things.

commentary.text: Hadith: The world/earth has been created for man and man has been created for the Hereafter.
FYI – The reference to the seven skies means this is a ‘Mutashabihat’ Ayat of the Quran. For additional context pls see remarks contained in my Introduction of the Quran.

translation.text: ˹Remember˺ when your Lord said to the angels, “I am going to place a successive ˹human˺ authority on earth.” They asked ˹Allah˺, “Will You place in it someone who will spread corruption there and shed blood while we glorify Your praises and proclaim Your holiness?” Allah responded, “I know what you do not know.”

commentary.text: A direct comparison is being made between (i) the Angels who are constantly/humbly worshipping Allah SWT (ii) and certain people who cause corruption and shed bloodshed on earth by virtue of the fact that man has been given intellect and freedom of choice. Angels only ask from curiosity
Allah SWT says He knows something that the Angels do not which is that although mankind will indeed cause corruption on earth, yet there are some who believe.
Lesson: Let’s understand our role on earth to be exemplary believers with humility and grace. Ameen.

translation.text: When We told the angels, ‘Bow down before Adam,’ they all bowed. But not Iblis, who refused and was arrogant: he was one of the disobedient.

commentary.text: Iblis was not an angel but a Jinn yet he was included in this command because of his previous behavior imitating the angles. He refused to bow down before Adam saying that he was created from fire while Adam from clay. The act of bowing down was symbolic gesture that showed obedience to Allah SWT.
Lesson: Where there is arrogance and or condescension; Satan is always present. Bowing to anyone is not an act that Muslims can do today to anyone other than Allah SWT.
Reflect: What happens when we neglect to perform sajdah or bow down?

translation.text: We cautioned, “O Adam! Live with your wife in Paradise and eat as freely as you please, but do not approach this tree, or else you will be wrongdoers.”

commentary.text: Lesson: The Garden/Paradise was expansive with only a single prohibition of a single tree, similarly, prohibitions, and restrictions in Islam are few, yet, some choose to focus only on them or break them. Everything is permitted in Islam unless prohibited.

translation.text: But Satan made them slip, and removed them from the state they were in. We said, ‘Get out, all of you! You are each other’s enemy. On earth you will have a place to stay and livelihood for a time.’

commentary.text: Lesson: Satan is the enemy of man. The sooner one understands and appreciates this fact the better.

arabic_lines: فَتَلَقّٰٓى اٰدَمُ مِنۡ رَّبِّهٖ كَلِمٰتٍ فَتَابَ عَلَيۡهِ​ؕ اِنَّهٗ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيۡمُ‏

translation.text: Then Adam received some words* from his Lord and He accepted his repentance: Surely He is the Accepter of Repentance, Most Merciful.

commentary.text: (Also see Surah 9:104 and 4:110)

The word ‘tawbah’ means to come back. Tawbah, on the part of man, signifies that he has given up his attitude of disobedience and returned to the submission and obedience of God. For repentance, three things are necessary: (i) acknowledgment of wrong (ii) giving up of wrong (ii) and a resolve to avoid the wrong/sin in the future.

Man's nature is weak therefore he has to return to Allah SWT again and again for forgiveness. So long as he does it sincerely, Allah SWT is the Accepter of Repentance, and Most Merciful التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيۡمُ‏ In fact, Allah SWT not only accepts man’s tawbah or repentance but changes the bad deeds into good.

Lesson: Mistakes were made by both Adam and Iblis, the difference being that Iblis showed extreme obstinate while Adam humbly begged for forgiveness. Allah SWT taught Adam the words for an apology and then accepted his repentance. (See below):

commentary.text: Allah SWT is addressing Adam, Hawa and Iblis after the incident in Paradise telling them to descend to earth. This is a direct warning and a reminder of the very serious consequences of denial.

extras.where: section intro before the unit's first line

How they resorted to treacheries and underhand conspiracies designed to create doubts and misgivings so as to frustrate the mission of the Prophet (PBUH). extras.text: The reason for choosing the Children of Israel as an example is that over thousands of years the changes of fortune which visit a people -- depending on whether they follow or refrain from following Divine Guidance --  were all conspicuous in the history of this nation, from which many lessons can be learnt.

translation.text: O Children of Israel! Remember ˹all˺ the favours I granted you and how I honoured you above the others.

commentary.text: (Also see 2:122)

translation.text: Guard yourselves against the Day on which no soul will be of help to another. No intercession will be accepted, no ransom taken, and no help will be given.

commentary.text: (Also see 2:123)
Israel is a Hebrew word meaning 'the servant/slave of Allah,’ it is also the second name of Prophet Yaqub (Jacob).

Jews here, are being addressed not as the "Children of Yaqub”, but as the "Children of Israel” so that the title may remind them that they are the children of the 'the servant of Allah' and therefore they should follow the example of their father in worshipping and obeying Allah SWT alone.

Allah SWT commands the Children of Israel to (1) remember His favours upon them (2) fulfill their promise with Allah SWT to embrace Islam and to follow Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) (3) fear Allah SWT only (4) believe in the Quran which is a continuation and confirms previous Scriptures (5) do not set a bad example by being the first and worst to deny (6) do not trade the Book of Allah for trivial worldly benefit/gain (7) do not knowingly change the Book of Allah by making additions or subtractions (8) establish prayer (9) give Zakat (10) pray in congregation (11) do not be of the hypocrites.
In quick succession from Ayat 47 till Ayat 60, Allah SWT lists the favors He bestowed on the Children of Israel.
God’s Favours upon the Israelites:
Favour 1)   Ayat 47: Honour.
Favour 2)   Ayat 49: Ending persecution by drowning Pharon and his army.
Favour 3)    Ayat 50: Parting of the Sea.
Favour 4)   Ayat 51: Forgiving Calf-Worship.
Favour 5)    Ayat 53: Revealing the Torah. Divine guidance.
Favour 6)   Ayat 54: A way to Forgiveness. Allah SWT in His Mercy provided a way to repent even in the face of great sins.
Favour 7)   Ayat 55: Forgiving the demand to see Allah SWT.
Favour 8)   Ayat 57: Shade and the Manna and the Quail. Tayyab and pure food from Allah SWT.
Favour 9)   Ayat 58: Permission to enter Jerusalem but humbly. Enter the gate in prostration.
Favour 10)  Ayat 60: Water for All – Twelve Springs.

translation.text: Indeed, the believers, Jews, Christians, and Sabians whoever ˹truly˺ believes in God and the Last Day and does good will have their reward with their Lord. And there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve.

commentary.text: IMAN + BELIEF IN THE NEXT LIFE + GOOD DEEDS = PARADISE

Believers here mean Muslims thus Muslims, Christians or Jews all who declare their belief in one God and last day will have their reward with Allah SWT. This Ayat captures the essence of faith and righteousness and extends a universal message of exclusivity and promise of reward for all those who sincerely believe in Allah SWT and the last day and who act righteously. We are remined of the profound Mercy of Allah SWT.
Note: None of Allah SWT Prophets or Scriptures contradict one another, so what Allah SWT revealed to Jesus (PBUH) is fundamentally same as He revealed to Musa (PBUH) and to Muhammad (PBUH).

Additionally, the aim of this Ayat is to negate the notion held by the Jews that just by virtue of their being Jews, they have a monopoly on salvation whereas all non-Jews are predestined to serve as fodder for hell-fire. To clarify this misgiving the Jews are told that what really matters in the sight of God is true faith and good deeds rather than any affiliation with a certain religious community.

sections.title: 67-71 THEIR ATTITUDE IN SACRIFICING A COW ON ALLAH'S COMMAND

translation.text: And ˹remember˺ when Moses said to his people, “Allah commands you to sacrifice a cow.” They replied, “Are you mocking us?” Moses responded, “I seek refuge in Allah from acting foolishly!”

extras.where: section intro before the unit's first line
section intro before the unit's first line
extras.text: This Surah is named after the cow in this story, which happened at the time of Musa (PBUH). A rich man was killed by his nephew -- his only heir -- and the body was thrown at the door of an innocent man. After a long investigation, no one was identified as the killer. Musa (PBUH) prayed for guidance and was told that the only way to find the killer was to sacrifice a cow and strike the victim with a piece of it. When this was done, the victim (dead man came alive for a short while) miraculously spoke and identified the killer.

translation.text: They said, “Call upon your Lord to clarify for us what type ˹of cow˺ it should be!” He replied, “Allah says, ‘The cow should neither be old nor young but in between. So do as you are commanded!’”

commentary.text: The Stubbornness of the Jews regarding the Cow

Allah SWT mentioned the stubbornness of the Children of Israel and excessive, unnecessary questions they asked their Messengers, such as, what should be the color, age, and look of the cow. (Ayat 68-70). Had they slaughtered a cow, any cow, it would have been sufficient for them. Instead, they made the matter difficult, and this is why Allah SWT made it even more difficult for them by being exacting in His specifications re: what kind of cow to slaughter.

Lesson: Questions and reflection are greatly encouraged in Islam so as to strengthen Iman, however, when one’s intent is suspect then instead of seeking clarification questions are aimed at evading and dodging the issue.
What do your questions reveal?

sections.title: 72 – 74 MIRACLE OF MAKING THE DEAD BODY ALIVE AND THEIR REACTION TO THE MIRACLE.

translation.text: So We instructed, “Strike the dead body with a piece of the cow.” This is how ˹easily˺ Allah brings the dead to life, showing you His signs so that you may understand.

Even then your hearts became hardened like a rock or even harder, for some rocks gush rivers; others split, spilling water; while others are humbled in awe of Allah. And Allah is never unaware of what you do.

commentary.text: Despite Allah SWT’s clear miracles and favours upon the Children of Israel they refused to believe and instead would make excuses and change religion to suit their needs/desires. Thus, we find that continuous sinning hardens the heart whereas softness of the heart comes with reflection of the Quran, and observing Allah SWT creations.
Parable of the heart is made with rocks.

Hadith: Do not talk too much without the remembrance of Allah. Indeed, excessive talking without remembrance of Allah SWT hardens the heart. Indeed, the furthest people from Allah SWT are the hard-hearted.

sections.title: 78 – 79 SOME OF THEM ATTRIBUTED THEIR OWN WRITINGS TO ALLAH

arabic_lines: وَمِنْهُمْ   أُمِّيُّونَ   لَا   يَعْلَمُونَ   ٱلْكِتَٰبَ   إِلَّآ   أَمَانِىَّ   وَإِنْ   هُمْ   إِلَّا   يَظُنُّونَ

translation.text: Some of them are uneducated and know the Scripture only through wishful thinking. They rely on guesswork.

So woe to those who distort the Scripture with their own hands then say, “This is from Allah”—seeking a fleeting gain! So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they have earned.

They say, ‘The Fire will only touch us for a few days.’ Say to them, ‘Have you received a promise from God– for God never breaks His promise– or are you saying things about Him of which you have no real knowledge?’

commentary.text: This was the state of the Jewish masses. They were ignorant of the Scriptures, unaware of the principles of faith as detailed by Allah SWT in His Book, unaware of the rules of conduct and teachings which are of fundamental importance for man's salvation. Because they lacked this knowledge, they fabricated a whole religion out of their desires and fancies, living in a paradise built on false hopes and illusions.
Above Ayat’s discuss common misconceptions, for example, assuming Hell is temporary. This is only wishful thinking as we have no knowledge of this fact from Allah SWT.

Lesson: Educate yourself!! Make learning the Quran a priority so that you do not have to rely on others or guesswork to get answers to the most important issues of your lives. Assess: How much do I understand?
Right of the Quran: (i) Believe in the Quran (ii) Understand the meaning (iii) Recite (iv) Reflect (v) Convey
Beware: Inventing or fabricating what is in the Quran or selective interpretation is a Huge sin with humiliation in this world and the worst punishment in the next life. (2:85).

arabic_lines: وَالَّذِيۡنَ اٰمَنُوۡا وَعَمِلُوا الصّٰلِحٰتِ اُولٰٓـئِكَ اَصۡحٰبُ الۡجَـنَّةِ ​​ۚ هُمۡ فِيۡهَا خٰلِدُوۡن‏

translation.text: those who believe and do righteous deeds are the people of the Garden, and there will they abide.

commentary.text: IMAN + GOOD DEEDS = PARADISE
Conversely now is a simple and oft repeated formula: Iman + Righteous deeds = Paradise.
But Iman must be followed by righteous deeds to get to Paradise, and similarly righteous deeds must be in conjunction with Iman to attain Paradise.
Genuine belief with consistent good deeds provides a clear pathway to success.

translation.text: But here you are, killing each other and expelling some of your people from their homes, aiding one another in sin and aggression; and when those ˹expelled˺ come to you as captives, you still ransom them—though expelling them was unlawful for you. commentary.text: LOSS IN THIS WORLD AND THE NEXT

sections.title: 94-96 JEWS' CLAIM OF EXCLUSIVE RIGHT TO INHERIT PARADISE IS PUT TO TEST

translation.text: Say to them, "If the abode of the Hereafter with Allah is exclusively reserved for you and not for the rest of mankind, then you should long for death, if you are sincere in your claim."

commentary.text: This was a litmus test for the Jews and it is just as relevant for us today.

The Jews claimed that they were the chosen people of the Lord and that Allah SWT had set aside blessings and favours of this world specially/exclusively only for them. And that Heaven is reserved for them.

Here Allah SWT challenges them that if they are so sure that their affairs are right with Allah SWT then this world should seem nothing but a liability or at the very least, they should have no desire to live a long life.

translation.text: But they will never long for death, because of what they have stored up with their own hands: God is fully aware of the evildoers.

commentary.text: But they (Jews) will never wish for death because of ‘what they have stored up with their own hands..’ means
as they have sinned excessively, they do not wish to meet with Allah SWT to suffer the consequences,
since all their effort, energy, money, goals, hopes, dreams are secured to this world they are greedy to live a long life.
Allah SWT knows what His servants are doing, whether good or evil, and will compensate accordingly.
Lesson: Evaluate what and where your efforts, money, hopes, aspirations are tied to? This world or the Next? Realize that Allah SWT is aware of all that we do so be sincere in faith.

sections.title: 104-105 ETIQUETTES TO ADDRESS THE PROPHET OF ALLAH SWT

arabic_lines: يٰٓاَيُّهَا الَّذِيۡنَ اٰمَنُوۡا لَا تَقُوۡلُوۡا رَاعِنَا وَ قُوۡلُوا انۡظُرۡنَا.…  ​

translation.text: O’ Believers, do not say [to the Prophet], ‘Ra_ina,’ but say, ‘Unzurna,’ and listen [to him]: an agonizing torment awaits those who ignore [God’s words].

commentary.text: Another crime of the Bani Isreal is being mentioned, yet, we Muslims are being told to pay attention.

The word Ra`ina رَ‌اعِنَا   is being referred to here and Muslims were asked to avoid using it.  When in conversation with the Prophet (PBUH) the Jews would mispronounce the word Ra`ina رَ‌اعِنَا   which meant 'kindly indulge us' or ' kindly lend an ear to us' and change it slightly to mean 'our shepherd.' Thus, Muslims are asked to avoid this word altogether and instead say ‘Unzurna’ انظُرْ‌نَا meaning, ‘I beg your pardon.’
Lastly, Muslims are asked to pay attention when listening to the Prophet (PBUH) so that he does not have to repeat himself.

Lesson: Allah SWT is, of course, teaching us the etiquette of listening and talking but just as importantly the lesson to move away from a situation that could become potentially volatile. A Muslim always means what he/she says.

Hadith: When they (disbelievers) would greet Muslims, they would say, `As-Samu alaykum,' meaning, `death be to you' instead of ‘As-Salam alyakum’ meaning ‘peace be upon you’. This is why we were commanded to answer them by saying, `Wa alaykum,' meaning, `and to you too', then our supplication against them shall be answered, rather than theirs against us.
*Believers pay attention whenever Allah SWT says يٰٓاَيُّهَا الَّذِيۡنَ اٰمَنُوۡ because something important is being mentioned.

commentary.text: Now the narrative turns to Ibrahim (PBUH) and the main subject is the new direction of the Qibla.
After Nuh (PBUH), Ibrahim (PBUH) was the first Prophet appointed by Allah SWT to spread the universal message of Islam.

Ibrahim's (PBUH) offspring descended from two main branches. (i) Children of Ismail, who lived in Arabia with the Quraysh and other Arabian tribes belonging to this branch of Ibrahim’s lineage. The other branch consisted of the (ii) Children of Ishaq. In this branch there arose a great number of Prophets, for example, Yaqub, Musa, Dawud, Sulieman, and Jesus. Since Yaqub was called Israel, his offspring came to be known as the Children of Israel.
The true mission of Ibrahim (PBUH) was to invite people to obey God and to construct the entire system of individual and collective life according to Divine Guidance.

While addressing the Children of Israel in the previous ten sections/rukus, Allah SWT set forth the criminal record of the Jews, exposing their decadent and ungrateful state at the time of the revelation of the Quran. Not only had they ceased to guide the world, but had completely turned away from Truth and righteousness.

At the same time, it is hinted that the non-Israelite communities who identified themselves with Ibrahim (PBUH) through Musa and Jesus had also veered far away from the way of Ibrahim (PBUH). They too did not deserve, therefore, to be entrusted with the religious leadership of the world.
Thus, religious leadership of all mankind is not an exclusive privilege of Ibrahimic blood.

By Allah SWT’s will a Prophet was then born of the Ishmaelites branch of the Ibrahimic family. The way advocated by this Prophet is exactly the same as that by Ibrahim, Isaac, Ismail, Yaqub and in fact all the Messengers.

This transfer of leadership naturally called for a change in the direction of Prayer. As long as the Israelites held the reins of the world's religious leadership, Jerusalem remained the center of the mission of Islam and the qibla. Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) as well as his followers had accepted Jerusalem as the qibla until God duly proclaimed the removal of the Jews from their position of leadership.

Ka'bah in Makkah was made the new qibla and since in the past it had been the center for Ibrahim (PBUH), it was difficult even for the polytheists and for the People of the Book to deny that the Ka'bah had a greater right to be made the qibla.

Ibrahim (PBUH) and his son Ismail (PBUH) were both reconstructing the Kaaba whose original foundations were laid by Adam (PBUH).
Even while performing this most blessed/sacred undertaking they were praying for acceptance of their good deed. They are working with fear, love and humility.
Lesson: We should never be satisfied with the good we do.

Let this be a warning to those Muslims who, being the descendants of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) or of a saint, delude themselves with the hope that their sins shall go unpunished in consideration of this privileged position. translation.text: The Jews say, "Become Jews and you will be rightly guided"; the Christians say, "Become Christians and you will have the true guidance." Say to them, "Nay, we turn away from every other way and accept the way of Abraham, and Abraham did not associate other gods with Allah."

commentary.text: Both the Jews and the Christians claimed to have a better right to the religion of Allah, than anyone else. The Jews said: ‘Our Prophet Musa (PBUH) is the best of Prophets, and our Scripture is the best of Scriptures and our religion is the best of religions’. They disbelieved in Jesus, the Gospel, Muhammad and the Quran.

The Christians on the other hand said: ‘Our Prophet Jesus is the best of Prophets, and our Scripture, the Gospel, is the best of Scriptures and our religion is the best of religions’. They disbelieved in Muhammad and the Quran. Both the Jews and Christians said to the believers: ‘Follow our religion, for there is no other true religion except ours’.

The Scriptures of the Jews and Christians attest to the fact that Ibrahim (PBUH) believed that worship, service and obedience are for Allah SWT exclusively. Since polytheistic elements made inroads into Judaism and Christianity it was obvious that both had strayed from the way of Ibrahim (PBUH).

All the Prophets sent by God invited mankind to the same Truth and to the same way. Just as importantly believe in all Allah SWT Scriptures.

items.text: Although at first read/glance it may seem a bit random, however, Juz 1 has a beautiful flow and purpose.

Firstly, it is a direct answer/response to Surah Fatihah re: the dua for guidance. Furthermore, it outlines all the characteristics, behaviors, qualities and traits (in this case specifically of the Children of Israel) that we should be careful not to emulate or repeat. A wise person learns from the mistakes of others.

The definition of a Believer, the concept of Tauhid as well as the purpose of our life has been beautifully articulated. Iman/faith is a gift that Allah SWT bestows. It is our duty as Muslims to value and protect this favour from Allah SWT so that we do not suffer the same fate as the Children of Israel.

Throughout the Quran Allah SWT has provided us with the definitions of success and failure. It is imperative that we understand how Allah SWT defines success and failure as opposed to inventing our own man-made criteria’s.

Appreciate, understand and recognize who your Master is. In the Quran, Allah SWT has described Himself via His attributes and names, such as, Accepter of Repentance and Most Merciful. Consequently, recognize what actions lead to His approval and love and which result in His anger and wrath.
Remember this world is temporary and death is a certainty, therefore, do not live on earth in a fog of delusion and confusion. Live a purposeful life that will lead to eternal success, in sha Allah.
Give Quran its due or its rights which is to: (i) Believe in the Quran (ii) Understand the meaning (iii) Recite (iv) Reflect (v) Convey.

These introductory Ayat’s declare the Quran to be the Book of Guidance and articulate the articles of the Faith -- belief in Allah, Prophethood and Life-after-death; divide mankind into three main groups with regard to its acceptance or rejection -- Believers, disbelievers and hypocrites. 1 – 20
Allah invites mankind to accept the Guidance voluntarily and to submit to Him, the Lord and the Creator of the Universe and to believe in the Quran, His Guidance, and in the Life-after-death. 21 – 29

The story of the appointment of Adam as Allah's Vicegerent on Earth, of his life in the Garden, of his falling a prey to the temptations of Satan, of his repentance and its acceptance, has been related to show to mankind (Adam's offspring), that the only right thing for them is to accept and follow the Guidance. This story also shows that the Guidance of Islam is the same that was given to Adam and that it is the original religion of mankind. 30 – 39

In this portion invitation to the Guidance has particularly been extended to the children of Israel and their past and present attitude has been criticized to show that the cause of their degradation was their deviation from the Guidance. 40 – 120

The Jews have been exhorted to follow Prophet Muhammad (Allah's peace be upon him) who had come with the same Guidance and who was a descendant and follower of Prophet Abraham whom they highly honoured as their ancestor, and professed to follow as a prophet. The story of the building of the Ka`abah by him has been mentioned because it was going to be made the qiblah of the Muslim Community. 121 – 141

In this portion, the declaration of the change of qiblah from the Temple (Jerusalem) to the Ka`abah (Makkah) has been made as a symbol of the change of leadership from the children of Israel to the Muslim Community, which has also been fore-warned to guard against those transgressions against the Guidance that had led to the deposition of the Jews. 142 – 152

In this portion practical measures have been prescribed to enable the Muslims to discharge the heavy responsibilities of the leadership that had been entrusted to them for the promulgation of Guidance. Salat, Fast, Zakat, Haj and Jihad have been prescribed for the moral training of the Ummat. The Believers have been exhorted to obey authority, to be just, to fulfill pledges, to observe treaties, to spend wealth etc., in the way of Allah. Laws, rules and regulations have been laid down for their organization, cohesion and conduct of day-to-day life and for the solution of social, economic, political and international problems; on the other hand, drinking, gambling, lending money on interest etc., have been prohibited to keep the Ummat safe from disintegration. In between these, the basic articles of the Faith have been reiterated at suitable places, for these alone can enable and support one to stick to the Guidance. 153 – 251

These verses serve as an introduction to the prohibition of lending money on interest. The true conception of Allah, Revelation and Life-after-death has been emphasized to keep alive the sense of accountability. The stories of Prophet Abraham (Allah's peace be upon him) and of the one who woke up after a sleep of hundred years have been related to show that Allah is All-Powerful and is able to raise the dead and call them to account. The Believers, therefore, should keep this fact in view and refrain from taking interest on money. 252 – 260

The theme of 153 - 251 has been resumed and the Believers have been exhorted to spend in the way of Allah in order to please Him alone. In contrast to this, they have been warned against the evils of lending money on interest. Instructions have also been given for the honest conduct of day-to-day business transactions. 261 – 283

The basic articles of the Faith have been recapitulated here at the end of the Surah, just as they were enunciated at its beginning. Then the Surah ends with a prayer which the Muslim Community needed very much at that time when they were encountering untold hardships in the propagation of the Guidance. 284 - 286
